newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany welcomes pact with U.S. on Cuba trade.
newsitem.headline: Germany welcomes pact with U.S. on Cuba trade.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt on Friday called a deal with the United States to end a transatlantic row over U.S. anti-Cuba laws a step in the right direction.

"It is important to me that we have found a way to enter into negotiations with the U.S. ovre the rejection of its unilateral extra-territorial measures. This is a step in the right direction," Rexrodt said in a statement.
The European Union earlier said that all 15 member states supported a plan that would end a disputes panel at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) over the so-called Helms-Burton act.
The act, an amalgam of U.S. anti-Cuba laws, has outraged Washington's trading partners because it threatens non-U.S. businesses with interests in Cuba.

France, Spain, Italy, Portugal and Belgium secured at Wednesday's meeting a clause that any backing of the deal be accompanied with the threat to reopen the WTO disputes panel if Washington took any action against EU companies.
The EU also restated its conclusions of July last year that the U.S. legislation towards Cuba, and other acts targeting Iran and Libya, were unacceptable both in law and principle.
"It is still unacceptable that a country aims to carry out its foreign policy goals by imposing sanctions against companies in third-party countries," he said.
"The agreement reached between the U.S. and the EU, however, represents an acceptable compromise," he added.
